proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(T(g)=\int_B g\,d\nu\) and
\[
\mathcal G_d(m)=\{g\in\mathcal F_d:A_dg=m\}.
\]
We first use the compact-fiber technique.  The domain \(S\) is compact by
\(\mathrm{ass:polygonal\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}support}\).  Every sequence in
\(\mathcal F_d\) is uniformly bounded by \(1\) and is equicontinuous with the
common modulus \(M_d\delta\), by \(\mathrm{def:surface\mbox{-}class}\).  To see
compactness without adding a hidden regularity condition, choose a countable dense
subset of \(S\), take a diagonal subsequence converging at every point of that
subset, and use a finite \(\delta\)-net together with the common modulus to show
that this subsequence is uniformly Cauchy.  Its uniform limit is continuous,
takes values in \([0,1]\), and satisfies the same Lipschitz inequality.  Hence
\(\mathcal F_d\) is compact in the uniform norm.  Moreover,
\[
 \lvert (A_dg)_j-(A_d\widetilde g)_j\rvert
 \leq \lVert g-\widetilde g\rVert_\infty,
 \qquad
 \lvert T(g)-T(\widetilde g)\rvert
 \leq \lVert g-\widetilde g\rVert_\infty,
\]
because every \(\mu_{dj}\) and \(\nu\) is a probability measure.  Thus \(A_d\)
and \(T\) are continuous.

Compatibility \(m_d\in K_d=A_d(\mathcal F_d)\), imposed by
\(\mathrm{ass:mean\mbox{-}compatibility}\), makes \(\mathcal G_d(m_d)\)
nonempty.  It is compact and convex, since it is a closed affine section of the
compact convex class \(\mathcal F_d\).  Therefore its image under \(T\) is a
compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R\), hence
\[
 T\{\mathcal G_d(m_d)\}=[L_d(m_d),U_d(m_d)],
\]
and both extrema are attained.  Since there is no cross-arm restriction, the
difference-image calculation gives
\[
\begin{split}
 I(m_0,m_1)
 &= [L_1(m_1),U_1(m_1)]-[L_0(m_0),U_0(m_0)]\\
 &= [L_1(m_1)-U_0(m_0),\ U_1(m_1)-L_0(m_0)].
\end{split}
\]
This also proves attainment of every intermediate value: every point in each
arm interval is the image of a convex combination of two feasible surfaces, and
the difference of two real intervals is the displayed interval.

It remains to distinguish this variational image from the causal identified set.
Let \(Y\in[0,1]\) be scalar, \(A\in\{0,1\}\),
\(X\in S\subset\mathbb R^2\), and let \(Z=(d,j)\) range over the finite observed
arm--cell labels.  The observable mean-information map sends a law of
\((Y,A,X,Z)\) to
\[
 \mathcal O(P)=\bigl(\{\mathcal L(X\mid Z=(d,j))=\mu_{dj}\}_{d,j},
                    \{\mathbb E[Y\mid Z=(d,j)]=m_{dj}\}_{d,j}\bigr).
\]
Define \(\Theta_I(\mathcal O(P))\) to be the values of \(\tau_B\) among all
potential-outcome laws satisfying the maintained range, Lipschitz, assignment,
and score-law restrictions and having this same observable summary.  Any such
law has conditional-mean surfaces in the two fibers, so the preceding argument
shows
\(\Theta_I(\mathcal O(P))\subseteq I(m_0,m_1)\).

For the reverse inclusion, fix any pair \((g_0,g_1)\) in the two fibers.  Choose
positive cell probabilities \(p_{dj}\) summing to one (or use the observed cell
shares when those are included in \(P\)); draw \(Z=(d,j)\) with probability
\(p_{dj}\), and draw \(X\mid Z=(d,j)\sim\mu_{dj}\).  The support, coverage,
disjointness, and boundary-null assumptions make this compatible with the sharp
side assignment \(A=d\) almost surely.  Independently draw
\(V_0,V_1\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\) conditional on \((X,Z)\), and set
\[
 Y(d)=\mathbf 1\{V_d\leq g_d(X)\},\qquad Y=Y(A).
\]
Then \(Y(d)\in[0,1]\),
\(\mathbb E[Y(d)\mid X]=g_d(X)\), and, for every observed cell,
\[
 \mathbb E[Y\mid Z=(d,j)]
 =\int_S g_d\,d\mu_{dj}=(A_dg_d)_j=m_{dj}.
\]
The causal target of this law is exactly \(\int_B(g_1-g_0)\,d\nu\).  Hence every
point of \(I(m_0,m_1)\) is generated by a bounded Bernoulli potential-outcome
law with the stipulated observed means.  This proves the reverse inclusion,
sharpness, and the asserted causal lifting.

Fix an arm and suppress its index where no ambiguity results.  Write
\(p=\sigma^+(S)\) and \(q=\sigma^-(S)\).  The compactness argument used for the
surface class in the sharp-set proof also shows that the maximum defining
\(H_M(\sigma)\) is attained, because
\[
 \left|\int_S(g-\widetilde g)\,d\sigma\right|
 \leq\lVert g-\widetilde g\rVert_\infty\,|\sigma|(S).
\]

We first use flat-metric scaling and partial transport.  Suppose \(M>0\), set
\(\phi=2g-1\), and push \(\sigma^+\) and \(\sigma^-\) forward under the dilation
\(x\mapsto 2Mx\).  The conditions \(0\leq g\leq1\) and
\(\operatorname{Lip}(g)\leq M\) become
\(\lVert\phi\rVert_\infty\leq1\) and
\(\operatorname{Lip}(\phi)\leq1\) on the dilated support.  Conversely, every
such restriction extends to Euclidean space by the McShane formula and can be
clipped to \([-1,1]\), so the restricted and global flat suprema agree.
Consequently the cited Piccoli--Rossi flat-duality lemma gives
\[
 H_M(\sigma)=\frac{p-q}{2}
 +\frac12 W_1^{1,1}(\overline\sigma^+,\overline\sigma^-),
\]
where bars denote the dilated pushforwards.  By the cited Piccoli--Rossi
submeasure formula, this generalized distance is minimized over equal-mass
submeasures.  If their common mass is \(t\), a coupling \(\pi\) of their
pullbacks satisfies
\[
 \lvert\sigma^+-\pi_1\rvert=p-t,\qquad
 \lvert\sigma^--\pi_2\rvert=q-t,
\]
and dilation multiplies the ordinary transport cost by \(2M\).  Substitution
therefore yields, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{split}
H_M(\sigma)
 &=\min_{\pi_1\leq\sigma^+,\,\pi_2\leq\sigma^-}
 \left\{\frac{p-q}{2}+\frac{p+q-2\pi(S\times S)}2
       +M\int\lVert x-y\rVert_2\,d\pi\right\}\\
 &=\min_{\pi\in\Pi_{\leq}(\sigma)}
 \left\{p-\pi(S\times S)
       +M\int\lVert x-y\rVert_2\,d\pi(x,y)\right\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus the clipping cost is unmatched positive mass plus transported distance;
there is no balance restriction on \(\sigma\).

For completeness, attainment of the displayed minimum does not rely on outer
multiplier attainment.  All feasible \(\pi\) have mass at most
\(\min\{p,q\}\).  On compact \(S\times S\), a diagonal subsequence argument
against a countable dense family of continuous test functions gives a weakly
convergent subsequence from every such sequence of measures.  Positivity and the
two marginal inequalities pass to the limit, while total mass and the integral
of the continuous distance cost converge.  Hence \(\Pi_{\leq}(\sigma)\) is
sequentially compact for this objective and the minimum is attained.  This also
supplies the transport-plan attainment implicit in the preceding scaling
calculation.  If \(M=0\), every class member is a constant \(c\in[0,1]\), so
\[
 H_0(\sigma)=\max_{0\leq c\leq1}c(p-q)=(p-q)_+.
\]
The transport expression has zero distance cost and is minimized by matching
mass \(\min\{p,q\}\), giving \(p-\min\{p,q\}=(p-q)_+\).  The identity therefore
holds for every \(M\geq0\).

We next use finite-dimensional separation to dualize the exact moments.  Let
\[
 \mathcal C=\{(A_dg,T(g)):g\in\mathcal F_d\}
 \subseteq \mathbb R^{|J_d|+1}.
\]
It is compact and convex.  For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) and every
\(g\) with \(A_dg=m_d\),
\[
 T(g)
 =\lambda^\top m_d+\int_S g\,d\left(\nu-\sum_j\lambda_j\mu_{dj}\right)
 \leq D_d(\lambda;m_d).
\]
Taking the primal maximum proves weak duality
\(U_d(m_d)\leq\inf_\lambda D_d(\lambda;m_d)\).

For the reverse inequality, put \(u=U_d(m_d)\) and fix \(\eta>0\).  The point
\((m_d,u+\eta)\) is outside \(\mathcal C\).  If \(z\in\mathcal C\) minimizes
its Euclidean distance to this point, convexity gives
\((m_d,u+\eta-z)^\top(c-z)\leq0\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\); hence a strictly
separating affine functional exists.  Write its coefficients as \((a,b)\).
Comparison with the point \((m_d,u)\in\mathcal C\) shows \(b\eta>0\), so
\(b>0\).  With \(\lambda=-a/b\), separation says
\[
 T(g)\leq u+\eta+\lambda^\top(A_dg-m_d)
 \quad\text{for every }g\in\mathcal F_d.
\]
Equivalently, \(D_d(\lambda;m_d)\leq u+\eta\).  Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\)
and combining with weak duality proves
\[
 U_d(m_d)=\inf_{\lambda_d\in\mathbb R^{|J_d|}}D_d(\lambda_d;m_d).
\]
The separating coefficient ranges over the whole Euclidean multiplier space;
at no step is \(\sum_j\lambda_{dj}=1\) imposed.

If \(r_d(m_d)>0\), work in the finite-dimensional affine space
\((m_d+E_d)\times\mathbb R\).  Apply the preceding normalized separation to
\((m_d,u+1/n)\), and take a convergent subsequence of its unit normals
\((a_n,b_n)\).  The limit \((a,b)\) supports \(\mathcal C\) at \((m_d,u)\).
It cannot have \(b=0\): otherwise
\(a^\top(v-m_d)\leq0\) for all \(v\in K_d\), while
\(m_d\pm r_d(m_d)a/\lVert a\rVert_2\in K_d\) would force \(a=0\), contradicting
unit normalization.  Thus \(b>0\), and \(\lambda_d=-a/b\), extended arbitrarily
from \(E_d\) to \(\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\), satisfies
\(D_d(\lambda_d;m_d)=u\).  This proves finite multiplier attainment on the
claimed relative-interior regime.

Reflection supplies the lower endpoint.  Since each cell law and \(\nu\) is a
probability measure, \(g\mapsto1-g\) is a bijection from the fiber at \(m_d\)
to the fiber at \(\mathbf1-m_d\), and
\(T(1-g)=1-T(g)\).  Hence
\[
 L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(\mathbf1-m_d).
\]

Finally consider the stated one-cell unit rectangle.  If \(m_d=0\),
nonnegativity and the positive uniform area law imply that a feasible continuous
surface vanishes everywhere on the rectangle and therefore on its boundary;
thus \(U_d(0)=0\).  For any finite scalar multiplier \(\lambda\), take
\(0<t\leq1\) and \(g_t(x,y)=(t-x)_+\) on the observed rectangle, extending it
to the rest of \(S\) by the clipped McShane formula.  It is \([0,1]\)-valued and
one-Lipschitz, and
\[
 \int_Bg_t\,d\nu=t,\qquad \int_Sg_t\,d\mu=\frac{t^2}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 D_d(\lambda;0)=H_1(\nu-\lambda\mu)
 \geq t-\frac{\lambda t^2}{2}>0
\]
by choosing any \(t>0\) when \(\lambda\leq0\), and
\(0<t<\min\{1,2/\lambda\}\) when \(\lambda>0\).  The dual value is nevertheless
zero by the value identity just proved.  Thus no finite multiplier attains the
infimum at this boundary mean, even though both the primal surface and every
inner partial-transport problem attain their optima.

We use one-dimensional symmetrization for the two rectangular cases.  Existence
of the stated two-dimensional uniform probability law entails \(a>0\), which
justifies division by \(a\).  In the uniform rectangle let
\[
 \bar g(x)=\int_0^1g(x,y)\,dy.
\]
Then \(0\leq\bar g\leq1\),
\(\lvert\bar g(x)-\bar g(x')\rvert\leq M_d\lvert x-x'\rvert\), its uniform
average on \([0,a]\) equals the cell mean, and
\(\bar g(0)=\int_Bg\,d\nu\).  Conversely, a one-dimensional function with
these properties gives the feasible surface \(g(x,y)=\bar g(x)\) on the cell,
and the clipped McShane formula extends it to the rest of \(S\) without changing
its values there.  Thus this reduction is exact, not an outer bound.

Fix a boundary height \(t\).  The Lipschitz and range restrictions imply
\[
 \bar g(x)\geq(t-M_dx)_+.
\]
Equality is feasible, and hence, for \(\ell_d=M_da>0\), the least possible cell
mean is
\[
\begin{split}
 \frac1a\int_0^a(t-M_dx)_+\,dx
 &=\frac{t^2-(t-M_da)_+^2}{2M_da}\\
 &=A_{\ell_d}(t).
\end{split}
\]
When \(\ell_d=0\), the function is constant and the least mean is \(t=A_0(t)\),
which explains the required zero-radius completion of the envelope definition.
Reflection around \(1/2\) shows that the greatest mean at height \(t\) is
\(1-A_{\ell_d}(1-t)\).  Convex combinations of the two extremizers keep their
boundary height and fill the interval between these mean values.  At the largest
feasible \(t<1\) the lower inequality binds, while \(t=1\) is feasible exactly
when \(m_d\geq A_{\ell_d}(1)\).  Therefore
\[
 U_d(m_d)=\max\{t\in[0,1]:A_{\ell_d}(t)\leq m_d\}.
\]
For \(\ell_d>0\), the envelope has the two branches
\[
 A_{\ell_d}(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 t^2/(2\ell_d),&t\leq\ell_d,\\
 t-\ell_d/2,&t\geq\ell_d.
 \end{cases}
\]
Inverting them, including the clipping point \(t=1\), gives
\[
U_d(m_d)=\begin{cases}
1,&m_d\geq A_{\ell_d}(1),\\
\sqrt{2\ell_dm_d},&m_d<A_{\ell_d}(1)\ \text{and }m_d\leq\ell_d/2,\\
m_d+\ell_d/2,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The same display remains correct at \(\ell_d=0\) under the corrected definition,
and reflection gives \(L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(1-m_d)\).

For the nonuniform rectangle the same reduction applies, now with horizontal
density \(\rho_\star\).  At height \(t\), direct integration of the extremal cone
\((t-x)_+\) gives
\[
 A_\star(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac32\int_0^t(t-x)\,dx=\frac{3t^2}{4},&0\leq t\leq\frac12,\\[6pt]
 \displaystyle\frac32\int_0^{1/2}(t-x)\,dx
 +\frac12\int_{1/2}^{t}(t-x)\,dx
 =\frac{t^2}{4}+\frac t2-\frac18,&\frac12\leq t\leq1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The transition means are \(A_\star(1/2)=3/16\) and
\(A_\star(1)=5/8\).  Solving \(A_\star(t)=m_d\) on the two branches and clipping
at one proves
\[
U_d(m_d)=\begin{cases}
\sqrt{4m_d/3},&0\leq m_d\leq3/16,\\
\sqrt{3/2+4m_d}-1,&3/16\leq m_d\leq5/8,\\
1,&5/8\leq m_d\leq1,
\end{cases}
\qquad L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(1-m_d).
\]

Finally use an explicit coupling for the triangle.  On the right-hand triangular
cell \(T=\{(x,y):x\geq0,\ x+y\leq1\}\), the uniform area density is \(2\).  The
projection \(P(x,y)=(0,y)\) has pushforward density
\[
 \int_0^{1-y}2\,dx=2(1-y)=w(0,y),
\]
so \(P_\#\mu_T=\nu\).  Since the centroid of \(T\) has first coordinate \(1/3\),
the Lipschitz inequality yields
\[
 \left|\int_Bg\,d\nu-\int_Tg\,d\mu_T\right|
 =\left|\int_T\{g(P(x,y))-g(x,y)\}\,d\mu_T\right|
 \leq M_d\int_Tx\,d\mu_T=\frac{M_d}{3}.
\]
The affine functions
\[
 g_+(x,y)=m_d+\frac{M_d}{3}-M_dx,
 \qquad
 g_-(x,y)=m_d-\frac{M_d}{3}+M_dx
\]
have cell mean \(m_d\) and boundary means \(m_d+M_d/3\) and
\(m_d-M_d/3\), respectively.  On \(T\), both remain in \([0,1]\) whenever
\(2M_d/3\leq m_d\leq1-2M_d/3\); this interval is nonempty when
\(0\leq M_d\leq3/4\).  Clipping their affine continuation to \([0,1]\) on all
of \(S\) preserves the Lipschitz constant and does not alter their values on
\(T\).  They attain the two coupling bounds, proving
\[
 [L_d(m_d),U_d(m_d)]=[m_d-M_d/3,m_d+M_d/3].
\]
Reflecting the horizontal coordinate proves the same formula for the left-hand
cell.  This completes all three exact reductions.

We first use geometric projection and compactness for the universal outer
program.  Because \(\mathcal T_h\) conforms to every cell and to \(B\), each
point of a cell belongs to a triangle contained in that cell and each point of
\(B\) belongs to a boundary edge of the triangulation.  A vertex of that triangle
or edge is at Euclidean distance at most its diameter, hence at most \(h\).
Nearest-node projection and lexicographic tie breaking therefore give
\[
 \lVert x-p_{dj,h}(x)\rVert_2\leq h,
 \qquad
 \lVert x-p_{B,h}(x)\rVert_2\leq h.
\]
For \(g_d\in\mathcal F_d\), put \(v_{d,h,z}=g_d(z)\).  Its nodal range and every
pairwise Lipschitz inequality hold, and pushforward gives
\[
\begin{split}
\left|\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\mu_{dj,h}(\{z\})-m_{dj}\right|
&=\left|\int\{g_d(p_{dj,h}(x))-g_d(x)\}\,d\mu_{dj}(x)\right|\leq M_dh,\\
\left|\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})-\int_Bg_d\,d\nu\right|
&\leq M_dh.
\end{split}
\]
Applying this to a primal optimizer proves
\(U_d(m_d)\leq V_{d,h}(m_d)+M_dh\).  Since \(U_d\leq1\), clipping the latter
quantity at one preserves the inequality, so \(U_d(m_d)\leq B_{d,h}(m_d)\).

For any feasible nodal vector, pairwise feasibility implies that the McShane
formula equals the prescribed value at every node; clipping does not change
those values.  Its extension \(e_h=E_{d,h}v_{d,h}\) belongs to \(\mathcal F_d\),
and the preceding pushforward argument, now combined with the relaxed moment
constraint, gives
\[
 \lVert A_de_h-m_d\rVert_2\leq2M_dh\sqrt{|J_d|},
 \qquad
 \left|\int_Be_h\,d\nu-\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})\right|\leq M_dh.
\]
Take atomic optimizers along any sequence \(h\downarrow0\).  Their extensions
are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous, so a subsequence converges uniformly
to some \(e\in\mathcal F_d\).  The last display implies \(A_de=m_d\), and the
atomic objectives converge along this subsequence to \(\int_Be\,d\nu\leq U_d(m_d)\).
Together with the already proved outer inequality this yields
\(B_{d,h}(m_d)\to U_d(m_d)\) for every compatible mean, including boundary means.

We now use relative-hull support functions to obtain the quantitative bounds.
Let \(m=m_d\), \(r=r_d(m)>0\), and \(q=A_de_h\).  If \(q\neq m\), write
\(v=(q-m)/\lVert q-m\rVert_2\).  Since \(m-rv\in K_d\) and
\[
 m=\frac r{r+\lVert q-m\rVert_2}q
   +\frac{\lVert q-m\rVert_2}{r+\lVert q-m\rVert_2}(m-rv),
\]
concavity and \(0\leq U_d\leq1\) imply
\[
 U_d(q)\leq U_d(m)+\frac{\lVert q-m\rVert_2}{r}.
\]
For an atomic optimizer, its objective is at most
\(\int_Be_h\,d\nu+M_dh\leq U_d(q)+M_dh\).  Adding the final \(M_dh\) in
\(B_{d,h}\), and using the residual bound, proves exactly
\[
0\leq B_{d,h}(m)-U_d(m)
\leq2M_dh\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m)}\right).
\]

For the inner program put \(K_{d,h}=A_d(\mathcal F_{d,h})\) and
\(\delta_h=\sqrt{|J_d|}\,\varepsilon_{d,h}\).  The finite nodal feasible set is
compact and convex.  Vertex range bounds extend over each triangle by
barycentricity, and integrating the bounded piecewise gradient along any segment
in convex \(S\) proves the global Euclidean Lipschitz bound.  Thus
\(\mathcal F_{d,h}\subseteq\mathcal F_d\) and \(K_{d,h}\) is compact and convex.
For every \(v\in E_d\),
uniformly approximating a support maximizer in \(\mathcal F_d\) gives
\[
 h_{K_{d,h}}(v)\geq h_{K_d}(v)-\delta_h\lVert v\rVert_2
 \geq v^\top m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\lVert v\rVert_2.
\]
If the ball \(m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\mathbb B_{E_d}\) were not contained in
\(K_{d,h}\), nearest-point separation inside \(m+E_d\) would contradict this
support inequality.  Hence the containment holds whenever \(\delta_h<r_d(m)\).

Let \(g^*\) attain \(U_d(m)\), and choose \(g_h\in\mathcal F_{d,h}\) with
\(\lVert g_h-g^*\rVert_\infty\leq\varepsilon_{d,h}\).  Write
\(e=A_dg_h-m\), so \(\lVert e\rVert_2\leq\delta_h\), and set
\(t=\delta_h/r_d(m)\).  If \(\delta_h=0\), \(g_h\) is already exactly feasible.
Otherwise
\[
 m-\frac{1-t}{t}e
 \in m+(r_d(m)-\delta_h)\mathbb B_{E_d}\subseteq K_{d,h}.
\]
Choose \(q_h\in\mathcal F_{d,h}\) with this moment and define
\(f_h=(1-t)g_h+tq_h\).  Then \(A_df_h=m\), and, using \(0\leq T(g^*),T(q_h)\leq1\),
\[
\begin{split}
 T(f_h)
 &\geq(1-t)\{U_d(m)-\varepsilon_{d,h}\}\\
 &\geq U_d(m)-\varepsilon_{d,h}-\frac{\delta_h}{r_d(m)}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus the exact-moment inner fiber is nonempty for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\(P_{d,h}(m)\leq U_d(m)\), and
\[
0\leq U_d(m)-P_{d,h}(m)
\leq\varepsilon_{d,h}\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m)}\right).
\]

It remains to verify the asserted approximation rate rather than assume it.
Every child in a midpoint refinement is similar to its parent, so the finitely
many shapes in the initial triangulation give a uniform shape constant over all
levels.  For
\(M_d>0\), extend \(g\in\mathcal F_d\) to a clipped \(M_d\)-Lipschitz function
on \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(Z\) be standard Gaussian in \(\mathbb R^2\), and put
\(u_\delta(x)=\mathbb E[g(x+\delta Z)]\).  The radial density of
\(\lVert Z\rVert_2\) is \(re^{-r^2/2}\mathbf1\{r\geq0\}\), whose first moment is
\(\sqrt{\pi/2}\).  Direct coupling gives
\[
 \lVert u_\delta-g\rVert_\infty
 \leq M_d\delta\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert_2
 =M_d\delta\sqrt{\pi/2}.
\]
Differentiating the convolution of the bounded weak gradient in a unit direction
and using
\(\mathbb E|Z_1|=2\int_0^\infty ze^{-z^2/2}dz/\sqrt{2\pi}=\sqrt{2/\pi}\)
gives
\[
 \lVert D^2u_\delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{M_d}{\delta}\mathbb E|Z_1|
 =\frac{M_d}{\delta}\sqrt{2/\pi}.
\]
Let \(I_hu_\delta\) be nodal affine interpolation.  If \(R_T\) has as rows the
two edge vectors of triangle \(T\), midpoint shape regularity makes
\(C=\sup_T h_T\lVert R_T^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}/\sqrt2<\infty\).  Taylor's
formula on the two edges and barycentric interpolation then give
\[
 \lVert\nabla I_hu_\delta\rVert_2\leq M_d(1+\theta),\qquad
 \lVert I_hu_\delta-u_\delta\rVert_\infty\leq M_dh,
 \qquad
 \theta=C\sqrt{2/\pi}\,h/\delta.
\]
The contraction
\[
 q_h=\frac12+\frac{I_hu_\delta-1/2}{1+\theta}
\]
is in \(\mathcal F_{d,h}\), preserves the range, and satisfies
\[
 \lVert q_h-g\rVert_\infty
 \leq M_d\delta\sqrt{\pi/2}+M_dh+\theta/2.
\]
Taking \(\delta=\sqrt h\) proves
\(\varepsilon_{d,h}=O(\sqrt h)\), with a constant depending only on the fixed
shape-regular initial mesh and \(M_d\).  When \(M_d=0\), constants are represented
exactly and \(\varepsilon_{d,h}=0\).  Finally, applying every construction to
\(1-g\) at moment \(\mathbf1-m_d\) gives the lower-endpoint programs.  Combining
the two armwise outward and inward endpoint errors gives the claimed shrinking
a posteriori effect-set gaps whenever the finite-program optimization errors
also vanish.

Apply the cited Hoeffding inequality to each cell and also to the negatives of
its observations.  Conditional on the fixed counts,
\[
 \Pr\{\lvert\widehat m_{dj}-m_{dj}\rvert>e_{dj}\}
 \leq2e^{-2n_{dj}e_{dj}^2}=\frac\gamma N.
\]
A union bound over the \(N\) cells gives
\[
 \Pr\{(m_0,m_1)\in Q_n\}\geq1-\gamma.
\]
Intersecting each coordinate interval with \([0,1]\) does not affect this event,
because every true mean lies in \([0,1]\).  On this simultaneous event, the
definition of \(C_n\) includes the entire interval \(I(m_0,m_1)\).  The bound is
distribution free over independent \([0,1]\)-valued cell observations, which
proves the displayed uniform infimum.

For the set identity, consider
\[
 \mathcal R_n=\{(g_0,g_1)\in\mathcal F_0\times\mathcal F_1:
                 (A_0g_0,A_1g_1)\in Q_n\}.
\]
It is a closed subset of a compact set and is convex because \(Q_n\) is a box.
When nonempty, the continuous effect map sends it to an attained compact
interval.  Partitioning \(\mathcal R_n\) by its moment vector and applying the
sharp mean-information theorem shows, in both directions, that this image is
\[
 \bigcup_{(q_0,q_1)\in Q_n\cap(K_0\times K_1)}I(q_0,q_1)=C_n.
\]

For consistency, the full-relative-dimension condition is essential.  Put
\(\Delta_{d,n}=\lVert\widehat m_d-m_d\rVert_2+sqrt{|J_d|}\max_je_{dj}\).
Independence and boundedness give
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert\widehat m_d-m_d\rVert_2^2
 =\sum_{j\in J_d}\operatorname{Var}(\widehat m_{dj})
 \leq\sum_{j\in J_d}\frac1{4n_{dj}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Because \(\Pr\{Z>\delta\}\leq\mathbb E[Z]/\delta\) for every nonnegative
\(Z\), this display and \(\max_je_{dj}\to0\) give
\(\Delta_{d,n}\to0\) in probability.  Since
\(E_d=\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) and \(r_d(m_d)>0\), the Euclidean ball
\(m_d+r_d(m_d)\mathbb B\) lies in \(K_d\).  Hence, with probability tending to
one, \(\widehat m_d\in K_d\), so the inversion is nonempty, and every
\(q_d\in Q_n\cap K_d\) satisfies \(\lVert q_d-m_d\rVert_2\leq\Delta_{d,n}\).

The concavity argument used in the relative-interior outer bound gives, for
\(q_d\in K_d\),
\[
 U_d(q_d)\leq U_d(m_d)+\frac{\lVert q_d-m_d\rVert_2}{r_d(m_d)}.
\]
When \(\lVert q_d-m_d\rVert_2<r_d(m_d)/2\), the point \(q_d\) itself contains a
relative ball of radius at least \(r_d(m_d)/2\); exchanging \(m_d\) and \(q_d\)
therefore gives the reverse bound with constant \(2/r_d(m_d)\).  Thus \(U_d\)
is locally Lipschitz at \(m_d\).  Reflection proves the same fact for \(L_d\).
The lower and upper endpoints of \(C_n\), which are extrema of combinations of
these four arm endpoint maps over the shrinking box, consequently converge in
probability to the two endpoints of \(I(m_0,m_1)\).  For compact real intervals,
Hausdorff distance is the maximum absolute difference of corresponding
endpoints, proving the claimed convergence.

If \(M_d=0\), every member of \(\mathcal F_d\) is a constant \(c\in[0,1]\).
Because every \(\mu_{dj}\) is a probability measure, compatibility is equivalent
to \(m_{dj}=c\) for every \(j\), and the boundary integral is also \(c\).  Hence
\(L_d(m_d)=U_d(m_d)=c\).

For the unit uniform rectangle, \(\ell_d=1\) and
\(A_1(1)=1/2\).  At \(m_d=1/2\), the closed form gives \(U_d=1\), while reflection
gives \(L_d=1-U_d(1/2)=0\).  Thus each arm interval is \([0,1]\), and the exact
difference interval is \([-1,1]\).

At \(m_1=7/8\), the same formula gives \(U_1=1\) and
\[
 L_1=1-U_1(1/8)=1-\sqrt{2(1/8)}=\frac12.
\]
At \(m_0=1/32\), it gives
\[
 U_0=\sqrt{2(1/32)}=\frac14,
 \qquad L_0=1-U_0(31/32)=0.
\]
Substitution into the sharp effect-set formula yields
\[
 I(m_0,m_1)=[L_1-U_0,U_1-L_0]=[1/4,1].
\]
All three reductions therefore follow from the proved endpoint formulas and the
sharp-set theorem.

theorem.statement:
Let \(S\) be a compact convex rational polygon, let the cells and \(B\) have
rational polygonal geometry, let every \(\mu_{dj}\) have a rational
piecewise-constant density, and let \(d\nu=w\,d\mathcal H^1\), where \(w\) is
nonnegative, normalized, and rational piecewise affine on \(B\).  If \(M_d\geq0\),
\(m_d\in K_d\), and \(\epsilon>0\) are rational and \(r_d(m_d)>0\), then there is
a terminating exact-arithmetic implementation of \(\mathsf{VPA}\) which returns
rational-nodal continuous piecewise-affine surfaces
\(q_d^U,q_d^L\in\mathcal F_d\) with \(A_dq_d^U=A_dq_d^L=m_d\), and rational
numbers
\[
 \underline U_d\leq U_d(m_d)\leq\overline U_d,
 \qquad
 \underline L_d\leq L_d(m_d)\leq\overline L_d,
\]
such that \(\overline U_d-\underline U_d\leq\epsilon\) and
\(\overline L_d-\underline L_d\leq\epsilon\).  The certificate verifies the
exact continuous cell integrals, nodal clipping inequalities, squared Euclidean
gradient inequalities, an atomic clipping-aware partial-transport plan, and the
continuous remainder \(M_dh(1+\lVert\lambda_d\rVert_1)\).  Thus the returned
rational intervals are outward enclosures, not floating-residual claims; no
bit-complexity bound is asserted.
theorem.proof_tex:
We give a terminating reconstruction-and-enclosure algorithm.  The technique is
dovetailed exact enumeration, with termination supplied by the already proved
relative-interior approximation and finite-multiplier attainment.

First record the exact finite representation.  On a rational conforming
triangulation, a piecewise-affine function is its nodal vector \(z\).  Because
the cell densities are rational and piecewise constant, exact integration gives
a rational matrix \(C_h\) with \(A_dq=C_hz\).  Range constraints are rational
linear inequalities.  On a triangle with rational edge matrix \(R_T\), the
condition \(\lVert\nabla q\rVert_2\leq M_d\) is, after squaring, a polynomial
inequality with rational coefficients in \(z\), because \(M_d\) is rational.
For a boundary subedge of length \(\ell\), endpoint function values \(z_0,z_1\),
and endpoint weight values \(w_0,w_1\), exact integration is
\[
 \ell\,\frac{(2w_0+w_1)z_0+(w_0+2w_1)z_1}{6}.
\]
All lengths are square roots of rationals.  Repeated rational bisection, checked
by integer squaring, supplies outward rational intervals of any requested width
for every finite sum and product appearing in the boundary objective.

We next prove that exact rational witnesses are dense in the relevant
piecewise-affine fiber.  The constant surface \(1/2\) has moment
\(c=\mathbf1/2\).  If \(m_d\neq c\), relative interior implies that for all
sufficiently small rational \(s>0\),
\[
 m'=\frac{m_d-sc}{1-s}
 =m_d+\frac{s}{1-s}(m_d-c)
\]
belongs to \(K_d\), indeed to its relative interior.  The exact-inner theorem
then supplies, on a sufficiently fine mesh, \(q'\in\mathcal F_{d,h}\) with
\(A_dq'=m'\).  The function \((1-s)q'+s/2\) has exact moment \(m_d\), nodal
values strictly between zero and one, and gradient norms strictly below \(M_d\).
If \(m_d=c\), the constant itself is strict when \(M_d>0\).  Thus the fiber has
a point strict in every range and gradient inequality.  Starting with a
near-optimal exact-inner point and mixing it by an arbitrarily small amount with
this strict point gives a strict exact-moment point with boundary value
arbitrarily close to \(U_d(m_d)\).

The affine solution space \(C_hz=m_d\) is defined over \(\mathbb Q\).  Gaussian
elimination gives a rational particular solution and a rational basis for its
nullspace.  Rational coefficients are dense in the free coordinates.  Therefore
every strict point in this affine space has rational points arbitrarily close to
it; strict inequalities persist under a sufficiently small perturbation.  It
follows that, for every \(\eta>0\), some mesh contains a rational nodal
\(q_d^U\) satisfying
\[
 A_dq_d^U=m_d,qquad q_d^U\in\mathcal F_d,qquad
 \int_Bq_d^U\,d\nu\geq U_d(m_d)-\eta.
\]
All these facts are exactly checkable from rational equalities and squared
inequalities.  When \(M_d=0\), compatibility and relative interior force
\(m_d=c_d\mathbf1\) with rational \(c_d\), and the constant surface \(c_d\)
solves both endpoints exactly.

For the upper certificate, enumerate rational multipliers \(\lambda_d\).  Their
density is sufficient because, for two multipliers,
\[
 \left|H_{M_d}\!\left(\nu-\sum_j\lambda_j\mu_{dj}\right)
       -H_{M_d}\!\left(\nu-\sum_j\lambda'_j\mu_{dj}\right)\right|
 \leq\sum_j|\lambda_j-\lambda'_j|,
\]
which follows from \(0\leq g\leq1\).  Since a finite optimal multiplier exists
at \(m_d\), rational multipliers attain dual values arbitrarily close to
\(U_d(m_d)\).

For a chosen rational \(\lambda_d\), form the atomic signed measure
\(\sigma_h=\nu_h-\sum_j\lambda_{dj}\mu_{dj,h}\).  Its masses are finite sums of
rational numbers and rational multiples of square roots of rationals.  The
Voronoi pieces defining the nearest-node pushforwards have rational linear
boundaries, so these expressions are obtained exactly by polygon and segment
integration.  Enumerate rational nonnegative matrices \(\pi\), and certify
\(\pi_1\leq\sigma_h^+\), \(\pi_2\leq\sigma_h^-\) using outward rational
intervals for the atomic masses.  For every certified plan, the partial-transport
identity gives the valid upper bound
\[
 H_{M_d}(\sigma_h)
 \leq \overline{\sigma_h^+(S)}-\pi(S\times S)
       +M_d\sum_{x,y}\pi_{xy}\,\overline{\lVert x-y\rVert_2}.
\]
These feasible rational plans approximate the atomic optimum.  Indeed, scale an
optimal real plan by \(1-\delta\), which creates strict slack at every positive
capacity, then approximate its finitely many entries by rationals; zero-capacity
rows and columns remain zero.  As \(\delta\downarrow0\), the resulting certified
costs converge to the atomic support value.  Rational bisection eventually
certifies every strict capacity inequality, even when a zero algebraic mass is
never assigned a sign.

The continuous remainder is proved directly, not inferred from a floating mesh
residual.  For every \(g\in\mathcal F_d\),
\[
\begin{split}
&\left|\int g\,d\left(\nu-\sum_j\lambda_{dj}\mu_{dj}\right)
-\int g\,d\left(\nu_h-\sum_j\lambda_{dj}\mu_{dj,h}\right)\right|\\
&\hspace{35mm}\leq M_dh\left(1+\lVert\lambda_d\rVert_1\right).
\end{split}
\]
Consequently the rational number obtained by outwardly rounding
\[
 \lambda_d^\top m_d+overline H_{d,h}
 +M_dh(1+\lVert\lambda_d\rVert_1)
\]
is a certified upper bound on \(U_d(m_d)\), while an outward lower rounding of
\(\int_Bq_d^U\,d\nu\) is a certified lower bound.

Now dovetail over the refinement level, denominators of rational nodal vectors,
denominators of multipliers and transport entries, and bisection precision.
Every finite candidate is checked in finitely many rational arithmetic steps.
Given \(\eta>0\), the rational primal-density argument supplies a lower bound
within \(\eta\) of \(U_d\); finite multiplier attainment, atomic convergence,
the displayed continuous remainder, and rational-plan density supply an upper
bound within \(3\eta\).  Taking \(4\eta<\epsilon\) proves that the dovetailing
eventually encounters a pair whose certified gap is at most \(\epsilon\), at
which point it terminates.

Finally, \(g\mapsto1-g\) maps the relative-interior fiber at \(m_d\) to that at
\(\mathbf1-m_d\), with the same radius.  Running the same procedure for
\(U_d(\mathbf1-m_d)\) and applying
\(L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(\mathbf1-m_d)\) gives \(q_d^L\) and the outward enclosure for
\(L_d\).

Here is the requested rational two-cell early-kill certificate.  Embed the
observed side \([0,1]\times[0,1]\) in
\(S=[-1,1]\times[0,1]\) with assignment boundary
\(B=\{0\}\times[0,1]\), and split the observed side into the two horizontal rectangles
\(C_1=[0,1]\times[0,1/2]\) and
\(C_2=[0,1]\times[1/2,1]\), use their uniform laws, put uniform \(\nu\) on
\(B\), and take \(M=1/2\) and
\(m=(1/2,1/2)\).  Small rational piecewise-affine tents supported in the two
cell interiors perturb the two moments independently while preserving strict
range and Lipschitz slack around the constant \(1/2\); hence \(m\) is an
interior point of the two-dimensional moment body.  For every feasible \(g\),
coupling \((x,y)\) to \((0,y)\) gives
\[
 \int_Bg\,d\nu-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^2\int g\,d\mu_j
 \leq M\int_0^1x\,dx=\frac14.
\]
The rational affine surface \(q^U(x,y)=3/4-x/2\) on the observed side has both
cell means \(1/2\), satisfies every squared gradient inequality with equality,
and has boundary mean \(3/4\); a clipped affine continuation gives a member of
the global class.  Thus \(U(m)=3/4\).  Reflection gives the exact lower witness
\(q^L(x,y)=1/4+x/2\) and \(L(m)=1/4\).

The exact multiplier \(\lambda=(1/2,1/2)\) has
\(\lambda^\top m=1/2\).  On refinement \(k\), let \(\bar h_k\) be any rational
outward upper bound on the maximum triangle diameter, chosen so that
\(\bar h_k\downarrow0\).  Push the preceding coupling through the cell and
boundary projections.  Its source and target move by at most \(\bar h_k\),
so its atomic mean distance is at most \(1/2+2\bar h_k\).  Cancelling common atomic mass
and applying finite flow decomposition produces a feasible partial-transport
plan with no larger cost; all of its masses are rational in this axis-aligned
instance.  Hence the atomic support is at most \(1/4+\bar h_k\).  The exactly verified
continuous remainder is
\(M\bar h_k(1+\lVert\lambda\rVert_1)=\bar h_k\), and therefore
\[
 \frac34\leq U(m)\leq\frac34+2\bar h_k,
 \qquad
 \frac14-2\bar h_k\leq L(m)\leq\frac14.
\]
These are rational outward enclosures with exact continuous primal moments and
gaps tending to zero on the prescribed dyadic refinement.  Thus the early-kill
instance passes without a floating residual.  This verifies every item in the
stated general certificate.  The enumeration may be slow, so the argument is a
termination theorem and deliberately makes no bit-complexity claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be finite nonnegative Radon measures on Euclidean
space, and define
\[
 d_{\mathrm{flat}}(\alpha,\beta)
 =\sup\left\{\int \phi\,d(\alpha-\beta):
       \lVert\phi\rVert_\infty\leq1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(\phi)\leq1\right\}.
\]
Then Piccoli and Rossi's generalized distance satisfies
\(W_1^{1,1}(\alpha,\beta)=d_{\mathrm{flat}}(\alpha,\beta)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:1304.7014, Definition 12 and Theorem 13, equation (11), accessed 2026-09-13.

added_lemmas.statement:
For finite nonnegative Radon measures \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), the value
\(W_1^{1,1}(\alpha,\beta)\) equals
\[
 \min_{\substack{\widetilde\alpha\leq\alpha,\ \,
                  \widetilde\beta\leq\beta\\
                  \lvert\widetilde\alpha\rvert=\lvert\widetilde\beta\rvert}}
 \left\{\lvert\alpha-\widetilde\alpha\rvert
       +\lvert\beta-\widetilde\beta\rvert
       +W_1(\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta)\right\},
\]
and the minimizing submeasures are attained.

added_lemmas.statement:
If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent and satisfy
\(a_i\leq X_i\leq b_i\) almost surely, then, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\mathbb EX_i)\geq t\right\}
 \leq \exp\left\{-\frac{2n^2t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n(b_i-a_i)^2}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent random variables such that \(a_i\leq X_i\leq b_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Then, if \(t>0\), \(\Pr\{\overline X-\mathbb E\overline X\geq t\}\leq\exp\{-2n^2t^2/\sum_{i=1}^n(b_i-a_i)^2\}\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under conditional cell-sample independence,
\[
\inf\Pr\{I(m_0,m_1)\subseteq C_n\}\geq1-\gamma,
\]
where the infimum ranges over all maintained bounded cell-outcome laws with the
fixed score laws and compatible means. Whenever
\(Q_n\cap(K_0\times K_1)\neq\varnothing\), \(C_n\) is an attained compact
interval equal to the effect image of all response-surface pairs whose joint
moment vector lies in \(Q_n\). If \(r_d(m_d)>0\) and
\(E_d=\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) for both arms, and
\(\min_{d,j}n_{dj}\to\infty\), then the Hausdorff distance between \(C_n\) and
\(I(m_0,m_1)\) converges to zero in probability.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original Hausdorff-consistency clause is false when the moment body has deficient affine rank: with \(M_d=0\) and two independently sampled cells, \(K_d\) is the diagonal segment and a shrinking coordinatewise box misses that affine hull with a probability that need not tend to zero. Requiring \(E_d=\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) is the precise rank condition under which relative-interior slack contains the random box center and makes the inversion nonempty with probability tending to one; the finite-sample whole-set coverage claim is unchanged.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(\ell_d=M_da\), define \(A_0(t)=t\), and, when \(\ell_d>0\), define
\(A_{\ell_d}(t)=[t^2-(t-\ell_d)_+^2]/(2\ell_d)\), for every \(t\in[0,1]\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The displayed envelope was undefined at the allowed value \(\ell_d=0\), although the closed-form theorem and the zero-smoothness sanity reduction quantify over that case. The exact zero-radius minimal mean at boundary height \(t\) is \(t\), so defining \(A_0(t)=t\) makes the construction total and preserves the theorem's piecewise inverse.

proposed.statement:
For every finite signed \(\sigma\) on \(S\),
\[
H_{M_d}(\sigma)=\min_{\pi\in\Pi_{\le}(\sigma)}\left\{\sigma^+(S)-\pi(S\times S)+M_d\int_{S\times S}\|x-y\|_2\,d\pi(x,y)\right\},
\]
and the minimum is attained. After the affine transformation \(\phi=2g_d-1\)
and the corresponding ground-metric rescaling, this support identity is
equivalent to Piccoli and Rossi's generalized \(W_1^{1,1}\) flat-metric dual.
For every \(m_d\in K_d\),
\[
U_d(m_d)=\inf_{\lambda_d\in\mathbb R^{|J_d|}}D_d(\lambda_d;m_d),\qquad
L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(\mathbf 1-m_d).
\]
No condition \(\sum_{j\in J_d}\lambda_{dj}=1\) is imposed. A finite minimizing
\(\lambda_d\) exists whenever \(r_d(m_d)>0\). In the one-cell unit-rectangle
specialization with uniform \(\mu_{dj}\), uniform boundary \(\nu\), \(M_d=1\),
and \(m_d=0\), the primal value is zero but every finite multiplier has strictly
positive dual objective, so multiplier attainment fails at that boundary mean.
proposed.justification: The theorem turns an infinite-dimensional clipped inverse problem into an evaluable partial-transport support cost while identifying the exact multiplier-attainment frontier needed for computation.
proposed.gap: Piccoli and Rossi's Theorem 13 has no exact areal side moments. Qiu and Stoye's equations \(2.1\)--\(2.3\) inform the bounded isotropic geometry, but their boundary-to-policy extrapolation problem has no areal moment operator or unrestricted cell-moment multipliers.
proposed.consumer: Certified endpoint software can use a transport flow at each multiplier and will not misdiagnose a boundary mean as a numerical optimization failure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the two published flat-metric facts used by the proof into the theorem's declared proof spine.

proposed.statement:
Under conditional cell-sample independence,
\[
\inf\Pr\{I(m_0,m_1)\subseteq C_n\}\geq1-\gamma,
\]
where the infimum ranges over all maintained bounded cell-outcome laws with the
fixed score laws and compatible means. Whenever
\(Q_n\cap(K_0\times K_1)\neq\varnothing\), \(C_n\) is an attained compact
interval equal to the effect image of all response-surface pairs whose joint
moment vector lies in \(Q_n\). If \(r_d(m_d)>0\) and
\(E_d=\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) for both arms, and

proposed.justification: The theorem covers both endpoints and every value in the sharp set without differentiating a potentially nonsmooth endpoint map.
proposed.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer give asymptotic criterion inversion, while Qiu and Stoye use an exact-normal approximation and Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu infer a point-valued boundary curve from unit-level data.
proposed.consumer: A sign certificate remains valid after simultaneous sampling uncertainty in every district-level stunting mean is propagated through identification.
